title: Touring theaters and clubs, and the dance routine
summary: Under Block's management they played theaters up the East Coast and in Chicago and clubs like the Southland in Boston, and Slim taught him dance steps for the act.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Uh-huh. So you -- then you all started working --
Started working, and Martin Block's management, he -- we got a chance to do quite a few things. We tried him and played theaters as far as Chicago and around
and about down South and what have you.
Now, were you working as part of a package, or were you working as an individual?
At times as part of a package, and at times we worked a couple of clubs. Like we worked, we went back up to Boston, and we worked a club called the Southland and --
Now, was the policy open the same way it was when you worked at the other clubs?

Yeah, oh, yes. Yes, it was real good, And we played theaters up and down the East Coast, went to Chicago. And we played a club out there, played a theater out there, the old Rum Boogie in Chicago, and it was quite an act we had. As time went by Slim taught me a couple of dance steps. He used to dance quite a bit, you know.
Would he dance and you accompany him or would he dance with the guitar?
No, he would dance with his guitar.

And I'd be playing. And at times when we had, when we were with a package, the orchestra we would put our instruments down and do a little dance routine, you know. And outside, other than that, just the two of us had, did our
little act, you know, guitar and bass.
